continuity_scope: Pan's Labyrinth / El laberinto del fauno, Guillermo del Toro's 2006 film continuity only. This pass uses British Film Institute and American Film Institute film records/authorized criticism and does not merge novelization or derivative works.
work_or_witnesses: Pan's Labyrinth / El laberinto del fauno, feature film (2006)
BFI official film record and BFI analysis/interview materials
AFI Catalog film record and AFI Movie Club context
coverage_rule: Include named individual dramatic characters supported by selected authoritative film materials: Ofelia, Captain Vidal, and Mercedes. The faun, Pale Man, fairies, labyrinth/underworld, trials, artifacts, places, political factions, and fantasy/reality ambiguity are terms or omissions unless a personal individual name is explicitly supplied.
omissions: All other characters and named fantastical figures are omitted where selected evidence provides only role/category terms or cast labels rather than a clearly individualized personal name.
Novelization, other derivative works, promotional interpretations beyond the selected film evidence, and any other continuity are separate witnesses.
Exact trial sequence, artifacts, fantasy ontology, all political/war details, outcome, and whether fantasy is literally real are not settled beyond the cited descriptions.

Child peril, fascist violence/torture, pregnancy/childbirth, torture, death, gender, and historical setting are flagged from BFI/AFI material without reproducing graphic details or flattening the film's fictional framing into historical fact.
uncertainties: BFI analysis explicitly frames fantasy/reality as a productive ambiguity or potential imagination; no definitive ontological claim is made.
The title's English Pan attribution is not used as a personal name: BFI's interview says the faun is not Pan and the name is absent from the original Spanish title.
The film is set against a Franco-era/Spanish Civil War aftermath backdrop in scholarly film framing; this research does not equate fictional characters or factions with any real individual or group.
No scene timestamps or full authorized screenplay were accessed; this is a curated archival/critical-film-record pass.
evidence_basis: BFI and AFI authoritative film records, criticism, and interview context only; no fan wiki, Wikipedia, novelization, uninspected script, or derivative material is used.
